slides.0.title: Central Valley II: Colchagua, Curicó and Maule
slides.0.subtitle: Apalta's icons, Curicó's rivers and Maule's old-vine Carignan
slides.1.title: Colchagua Valley
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Location and sub-areas
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The southern half of the Rapel DO, about 130 km south of Santiago, with sub-areas and communes such as Apalta, Marchigüe and Lolol (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth's regions page says Colchagua has Chile's largest Carmenère plantings and is also known for full-bodied Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Transversal zones (figures vary)
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wine With Seth's Colchagua page: Costa 100–300 m, Entre Cordilleras 200–500 m, Andes 400–800 m (anchored by the Apalta amphitheatre); the same page also gives 100–500 m overall, so it is not tested
slides.1.content: Colchagua is Rapel's southern half, known for Carmenère and full-bodied reds.
slides.2.title: Apalta and the emerging sub-areas
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Apalta
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Decanter: a dry climate with big temperature swings suited to Bordeaux varieties; Montes' hillside Carmenère grows on rocky clay. Wine With Seth: decomposed granite soils on north-facing slopes
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Clos Apalta
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Lapostolle was founded in 1994 and Clos Apalta's first vintage was 1997; the 2005 was named Wine Spectator's 2008 Wine of the Year (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Marchigüe and Lolol
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Decanter: Marchigüe has clay soils and Montes calls it "the Chilean Pomerol", planting Merlot; Lolol shows potential for Carmenère on poor soils near the ocean
slides.2.content: Apalta is Colchagua's star, with Marchigüe and Lolol as emerging sub-areas.
slides.3.title: Curicó Valley
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Rivers and location
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Between Colchagua and Maule; the Teno and Lontué rivers join near Curicó to form the Mataquito River (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Sub-areas and grapes
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Teno (west, around the town of Curicó) and Lontué (east, around Molina); about 19,000 ha with 600–700 mm of annual rain, led by Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: History
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Miguel Torres Chile was founded in 1979; San Pedro in 1865 and Valdivieso in 1879 (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: Curicó's sub-areas are named for the Teno and Lontué rivers, and it is where Torres set up in Chile.
slides.4.title: Maule Valley and VIGNO
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Location and climate
slides.4.highlights.0.content: About 250 km south of Santiago at the southern end of the Central Valley; a Mediterranean climate with about 735 mm of rain a year, one of Chile's cooler regions, moderated by the east–west Maule River (Wikipedia)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Plantings (c. 2013)
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Wikipedia's table: Cabernet Sauvignon 14,475 ha, Chardonnay 4,631, Mission (País) 3,364, Sauvignon Blanc 2,838, Merlot 2,137, Carmenère 2,045, Syrah 1,182, Carignan 377; the page's total of 785 ha does not fit the table, so it is not tested
slides.4.highlights.2.title: VIGNO
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Vignadores de Carignan took shape in 2010–2011 (Wine Anorak says a collective formed in 2010, Decanter says it was founded in 2011); dry-farmed old-vine Carignan from Maule, vines at least 30 years old, two years' ageing before release. Sources give different minimum Carignan shares (65%, 70%, 85%), so this is not tested
slides.4.content: Maule is known for a cooler climate, dry-farmed old vines and VIGNO.
Which half of the Rapel Valley DO is Colchagua?
D. It is not part of Rapel
Which variety does Wine With Seth say has its largest Chilean plantings in Colchagua?
As stated on the regions page.
Clos Apalta belongs to which winery?
Lapostolle was founded in 1994, first vintage 1997.
In which year was Miguel Torres Chile founded?
What vine age does VIGNO require for its Carignan?
The vines must also be dry-farmed, with two years' ageing before release.
